shop.description: A shop: `shop.toml`, at the top of the shop's directory.  Its machines, tools, tooling and materials are the files in the directories beside it (`SHOP_DIRECTORIES`); the reader fills in `machines`, `tools`, `tooling` and `materials` from them, so `shop.toml` itself has none of them.

units.description: The units the shop prefers: `in` (imperial) or `mm` (metric).  One of: in, mm.

machine_kinds.description: The kinds of machines the shop has, computer controlled or manual (for prep work).  One of: cnc_mill, cnc_router, cnc_lathe, laser_cutter, 3d_printer, manual_mill, manual_lathe, manual_drill_press, manual_bandsaw.

machines.description: The machines in the shop: the files in `machines/`.

tools.description: The tools on hand, shared by the machines: the files in `tools/`.

tooling.description: The work holding on hand (grid plates for now), shared by the machines: the files in `tooling/`.

materials.description: The materials it cuts, and how to drill and mill them: the files in `stock_materials/`.

tool_materials.description: What its tools are made of, and how fast each cuts: the files in `tool_materials/`.

location.description: Where a shop is.  Every key is optional, since a shop on a boat may have none.

controller.description: The controller of a machine (e.g. LinuxCNC), and how its G-code is written.  LinuxCNC is the baseline.  (To come: every code it accepts, its canned cycles, and tool length offsets.)  `tool_change` is a Python `str.format()` template, filled in with the tool's `number` and `description`; it may hold several lines, each words or a whole-line comment, such as a `(MSG, ...)` line and `M0`, so the operator is told which tool to put in.

tool_table.description: The tools loaded in one machine: T numbers (1 to 99) and the names of the tools in them.  Each is unique: no T number twice, and no tool twice, here or in any other machine's tool table (a tool is in one machine at a time).  It is in its machine's file, as `[tool_table.tools]`.

tools.description: Tools: the bits that go in a holder in the spindle.  How to cut with each (`rpm`, `feed`, `plunge`) is given with the tool for now, until it can be worked out from the material being cut.  Only the bits are described; `holder` only says what holds each one.  Tools are shared by machines, so they are not listed by machine: a machine's `tool_table` names the ones it has loaded, and every tool's `name` and `unique_id` are unique among all the tools (T numbers are only unique within one machine).
